name: String Encoding & Decoding — Base64, Hex, ROT13 & Cipher Identification
description: Decoding encoded strings found in obfuscated JavaScript or server responses. Three main types: (1) Base64 — alphanumeric + '=', ends with == or =, echo ... | base64 -d; (2) Hex — 0-9 a-f pairs only, echo ... | xxd -p -r; (3) ROT13/Caesar — letters only shifted 13 chars, echo ... | tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'. Cipher identification: Cipher Identifier at boxentriq.com. Pattern: spot by format → decode → use decoded value in subsequent curl POST request.
notes:
=== WHY ENCODING IN OBFUSCATED JS ===
Obfuscated scripts commonly encode strings/data to:
  → Evade string-based IDS/AV detection
  → Hide C2 URLs, API keys, payloads
  → Make static analysis harder
Encoding ≠ Encryption: encoding is reversible without a key
Encryption DOES require a key (much harder to reverse)

=== BASE64 ===
Identifying base64:
  → Only contains: A-Z a-z 0-9 + / =
  → String length is multiple of 4 (padded with = signs)
  → Ends with = or == (padding)
  → Example: ZG8gdGhlIGV4ZXJjaXNlCg==

Encode:
  echo 'https://www.hackthebox.eu/' | base64
  → Output: aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaGFja3RoZWJveC5ldS8K

Decode:
  echo 'aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaGFja3RoZWJveC5ldS8K' | base64 -d
  → Output: https://www.hackthebox.eu/

Decode without trailing newline:
  echo -n 'aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaGFja3RoZWJveC5ldS8K' | base64 -d

Decode file:
  base64 -d encoded.txt > decoded.txt

Online: https://www.base64decode.org/

=== HEX ENCODING ===
Identifying hex:
  → Only contains: 0-9 and a-f (16 chars total)
  → Always even number of characters (each byte = 2 hex chars)
  → Example: 68747470733a2f2f7777772e6861636b746865626f782e65752f

Encode to hex:
  echo 'https://www.hackthebox.eu/' | xxd -p
  → 68747470733a2f2f7777772e6861636b746865626f782e65752f0a

Decode hex:
  echo '68747470733a2f2f7777772e6861636b746865626f782e65752f0a' | xxd -p -r
  → https://www.hackthebox.eu/

  xxd -p -r = plain hex reverse (decode)
  xxd -p    = plain hex forward (encode)

Alternative decode with Python:
  python3 -c "print(bytes.fromhex('68747470733a2f2f7777772e6861636b746865626f782e65752f').decode())"

Alternative decode with printf:
  printf '%b' "$(echo '68747470733a...' | sed 's/\(..\)/\\x\1/g')"

=== ROT13 / CAESAR CIPHER ===
Identifying ROT13:
  → All characters are letters only (no numbers)
  → Letter frequency looks random but 'http://' → 'uggc://' (recognizable pattern)
  → Example: uggcf://jjj.unpxgurobk.rh/ = https://www.hackthebox.eu/
  → 'ROT' + number = how many positions each letter is shifted
  → ROT13 is self-inverse (apply twice = original)

Encode ROT13 (same command as decode!):
  echo 'https://www.hackthebox.eu/' | tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'
  → uggcf://jjj.unpxgurobk.rh/

Decode ROT13:
  echo 'uggcf://jjj.unpxgurobk.rh/' | tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'
  → https://www.hackthebox.eu/

tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m' explanation:
  A→N, B→O, ..., M→Z, N→A, O→B, ..., Z→M (shift 13)
  Same mapping for lowercase a-z

Online: https://rot13.com/

Other Caesar shifts:
  ROT1:  echo 'text' | tr 'A-Za-z' 'B-ZAb-za'
  ROT5 (digits): echo '12345' | tr '0-9' '5-90-4'
  ROT18 (letters+digits): combine ROT13+ROT5

=== IDENTIFYING UNKNOWN ENCODING ===
Cipher Identifier: https://www.boxentriq.com/code-breaking/cipher-identifier
  → Paste encoded string → auto-detects encoding type
  → Works for: base64, hex, rot13, morse, binary, etc.

Determtination guide:
  Is it only letters? → ROT13 / Caesar cipher
  Is it 0-9 and a-f? → Hex
  Is it alphanumeric + = ? → Base64
  Is it only [ ] ( ) ! + ? → JSFuck
  Is it % followed by hex? → URL encoding (%20 = space)
  Is it &#number; ? → HTML entity encoding

URL decode Python:
  python3 -c "from urllib.parse import unquote; print(unquote('Hello%20World'))"

=== COMPLETE WORKFLOW EXAMPLE ===
1. Fetch the JS:
   curl -s http://<TARGET>:<PORT>/secret.js

2. Identify obfuscation: eval(function(p,a,c,k,e,d)... = packed

3. Deobfuscate at UnPacker → get:
   function generateSerial() {
     var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest;
     var url = '/serial.php';
     xhr.open('POST', url, true);
     xhr.send(null);
   }

4. Replicate JS function:
   curl -s http://<TARGET>:<PORT>/serial.php -X POST
   → Response: ZG8gdGhlIGV4ZXJjaXNlLCBkb24ndCBjb3B5IGFuZCBwYXN0ZSA7KQo=

5. Identify encoding: ends with '=', alphanumeric → Base64

6. Decode:
   echo 'ZG8gdGhlIGV4ZXJjaXNlLCBkb24ndCBjb3B5IGFuZCBwYXN0ZSA7KQo=' | base64 -d
   → 'do the exercise, don't copy and paste ;)'

7. Send decoded value as POST param:
   curl -s http://<TARGET>:<PORT>/serial.php -X POST -d 'serial=DECODED_VALUE'
   → Get flag!
